title: Chamier’s ‘all the justified have this faith’ proof proves too much — election parallel
source_text: CIV. Nec tollit difficultatem quod dicit Chamierus, fidem dici justificare, quia omnes justificati, tandem ejus participes fiunt; nec in ullo reperitur qui non sit justificatus. Nam sic quoque dici possemus per fidem & bona opera electi esse ad gratiam: quia in omnibus electis ad gratiam reperiuntur tandem fides & bona opera, nec fides & bona opera in ullo reperiuntur, qui non sit etiam ad gratiam electus.
pass_a_gloss: Nor does it remove the difficulty what Chamier says, that faith is said to justify because all the justified at length become partakers of it; nor is it found in anyone who is not justified. For so also we could be said to have been elected to grace through faith and good works: because in all the elect to grace faith and good works are at length found, nor are faith and good works found in anyone who is not also elected to grace.
pass_b_english: Chamier’s escape: faith “justifies” because every justified person eventually has this faith, and no one has it who is not justified.

Le Blanc: that proves too much — by the same logic we could say we are elected to grace through faith and good works, since every elect person eventually has them, and no one has them who is not elect.
